A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the elderly population, as compared with a young population, tend to adopt different motor strategies in the execution of a sit-to-stand task.
elderly people tend to adopt motor strategies that are more economical, but less effective than the young ones.
the elderly subjects, as compared to young ones, tended to adopt a motor strategy characterised by a lower functional reserve, but with a higher safety margin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a subject-specific approach, which takes into account the individual's functional constraints, is necessary in order to identify the motor strategies used to achieve a certain motor task.
